monthly_review.summary: This month shows a marked reduction in training volume and intensity compared to last month, with lower total km, fewer runs, slower average pace, and significantly less time spent in higher HR zones — indicating a deliberate or unintentional downshift toward recovery or base-building.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3+ time dropped from 45% of total HR time last month (z3+z4+z5 = 26+15+4) to just 13% this month (z3+z4+z5 = 12+1+0), signaling a major shift away from threshold and VO2 max stimulus.

goal_tracker.message: You need 21.1 more km across 6 sessions in the remaining 21 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~3.5 km per session. Prioritizing consistency over distance (e.g., 4–5 shorter Zone 2 runs + 1 longer run) will support sustainability.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.1 m/km per bpm, even though average HR decreased by 12 bpm — suggesting reduced running economy or pacing inconsistency, particularly evident in the 9.5 km run where stride length dropped to 66.49 cm and ground contact increased to 351 ms.

insights.title: Near-total absence of high-intensity stimulus
insights.body: This month includes zero time in Zone 5 and only 1% in Zone 4 — compared to 4% and 15% respectively last month — meaning no meaningful VO2 max or anaerobic capacity work occurred recently.

insights.title: Stride length and ground contact variability signal fatigue or pacing mismatch
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 66.49 cm (9.5 km run) to 88.65 cm (2.3 km run), while ground contact varied from 301–351 ms; the longest run showed the shortest stride and longest contact — classic signs of late-run fatigue or insufficient aerobic endurance at that duration.

insights.title: Very low HR and high-efficiency run on 2026-05-05 suggests effective active recovery
insights.body: The 2.8 km run at 121 bpm (Z1), 10:07 min/km, and 144 spm achieved 2.0 aerobic TE with minimal stress — aligning well with recovery physiology and demonstrating good Z1 discipline.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run tomorrow (HR 125–135 bpm) at consistent 8:30–9:00 min/km pace, focusing on maintaining stride length ≥80 cm (use real-time cadence/stride feedback if available)
recommendations.reason: Your recent Zone 2 runs average 139 spm but show declining stride length under duration — reinforcing form at moderate effort rebuilds neuromuscular efficiency without adding load.

recommendations.action: Insert one 20-min Zone 3 interval session before May 20: 4 x 5-min @ HR 145–152 bpm with 90-sec Z1 jog recovery
recommendations.reason: Last month included 26% Zone 3 time and best pace of 428 sec/km (7:08); reintroducing controlled threshold work will re-stimulate lactate buffering and prevent aerobic decay.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 2.8 km Z1 recovery run (2026-05-05) on May 12 — same HR target (<125 bpm), pace (~10:07 min/km), and focus on cadence ≥144 spm and vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: That run delivered optimal recovery stimulus (TE 2.0, low HR, stable VO2 max) and provides a reproducible benchmark for managing fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish consistent Zone 2 rhythm, rebuild stride integrity at sustainable efforts, and reintroduce one targeted Zone 3 stimulus to maintain threshold fitness without overstressing recovery capacity.
